correctness.rationale: For all n>=3 and m>=2, full dihedral-by-clique symmetry averaging is lossless by convexity. Exactly three signed spectral gap inequalities follow from the tensor-sum Laplacian. The two derived upper bounds are attained simultaneously by a=Gamma/s, b=Gamma/m; active equality forces uniqueness in the invariant class. Trigonometric threshold and heuristic asymptotics were algebraically checked, and 220 numerical LP checks plus 60 dense spectra agreed. Finite tests supplement rather than replace the proof; no unrestricted uniqueness claimed.

value.rationale: The exact solution covers two unbounded graph parameters, a parity-sensitive discrete threshold, uniqueness among invariant solutions and an explicit globally optimal chain. The saturated odd-layer 7-to-8 transition is not a routine degree count, but a competition between a signed spectral extremum and a stochastic row budget. The spectral gap improvement over uniform-edge Metropolis grows linearly as (m+1)/2 at fixed clique size in long cycles, while even prisms reveal a periodicity obstruction.
